A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MotherNet by the same authors. All 17 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures despite substantial revision and a changed title.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, runtime, distillation, synthetic failure-case and data-leakage experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original MotherNet evaluations, including fine-tuning experiments and results on TabZilla. The attribution of TabZilla comparator results to prior work does not negate these original results.

M1.justification: v1 uses learned-query attention to produce a 2048-dimensional dataset embedding; v2 replaces this with class-wise average embeddings totaling 512 × 10 dimensions. The reported model size changes from 149M to 89M parameters. This changes a central architectural component, while retaining the meta-training objective and two-hidden-layer, low-rank child network.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on TabZilla, including larger source datasets beyond the earlier small-dataset coverage. The original 30 CC-18 test datasets, 149 validation datasets and synthetic failure-task families remain; their relocation does not constitute new coverage.

E2.justification: The CC-18 comparison adds ResNet and HyperFast variants and removes the separately retrained TabPFN comparator. The validation comparison also drops the tuned MLP. TabZilla introduces reported comparisons with methods such as CatBoost, SAINT, NODE and FTTransformer, using comparator results attributed to McElfresh et al.

E3.justification: MotherNet changes from three ensemble members with optional Yeo-Johnson transformation to eight members incorporating optional categorical one-hot and continuous quantile encoding. Reported tuning-budget sweeps are replaced by one-hour comparisons. New protocols include fine-tuning controls, 3000-point subsampling for TabZilla, normalized accuracy and timing per 1000 points. CC-18's 50/50 split and ROC-AUC metric remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds explicit ensembling and gradient-descent fine-tuning analyses in Section 4.1. Its validation error analysis changes from a 0.1 TabPFN–XGBoost gap to a 0.05 MotherNet–XGBoost gap. Synthetic failure analyses remain, with an unexplained additional Boolean-prior curve in Figure 6, but v1's ID-only Random Forest leakage-confirmation experiments are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five CC-18 splits with standard deviations and use critical-difference diagrams. Both specify 20 synthetic datasets per complexity level with five-fold stratified cross-validation. Additional tables and significance findings do not establish a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased repetition count.

E6.justification: Substantial result entries are added or replaced. v1 ranks MotherNet behind XGBoost and MLP-distill; v2 Table 1 ranks it ahead of XGBoost but behind MLP-distill under revised configurations and comparator membership. New TabZilla results include MotherNet's normalized AUC of 0.84 ± 0.18 and mean rank of 8.30. Fine-tuning results and absolute runtime tables also expand the evidence; these are not controlled same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The meta-training objective in Equation 1, synthetic-prior assumptions and appendix Boolean-task construction remain unchanged. v2 writes out layerwise formulas for the already-described low-rank child MLP, without introducing a new theoretical result, proof or substantive formal argument.

C1.justification: The central claim—generating competitive, fast child networks without dataset-specific gradient descent—remains. v2 adds a prominent claim that HyperFast depends on fine-tuning and hyperparameter tuning on small datasets, and qualifies its novelty comparison from existing hypernetworks generally to most existing hypernetworks.

C2.justification: The learned-regularization explanation and discontinuity/Boolean failure mechanisms remain. v2 adds the hypothesis that fine-tuning undermines learned regularization, identifies categorical-encoding sensitivity, and clarifies that processing larger datasets does not establish their predictive accuracy. It also discusses HyperFast training-set overlap and TabZilla's unequal data and hardware conditions.

D1.justification: Unlike v1, v2 announces and links public training code, inference code and pretrained weights, materially improving documented access to the expensive pretrained model. It also adds ResNet search-space details, fine-tuning variables and hardware qualifications for TabZilla. The removed custom-TabPFN comparison takes its training recipe with it.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around HyperFast, Conditional Neural Processes, Transformer Neural Processes and HyperTransformer. It adds relevant LLM-for-tabular and TabZilla literature while removing much of v1's foundation-model, MAML/CAVIA and classical meta-learning discussion. These changes alter the comparison with closely related approaches, beyond bibliography maintenance.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. Distillation moves after MotherNet's method description, failure-case discussion moves into the appendices, and a separate limitations section precedes the conclusion. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a single-column conference layout, redraws the architecture diagram, combines score and critical-difference displays, and removes tuning-budget curves. It adds detailed performance/runtime tables and a runtime–accuracy plot, replaces per-dataset charts with tables, and relocates dataset inventories and failure illustrations.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny through a second benchmark, direct HyperFast comparisons and explicit fine-tuning controls, addressing v1's narrower comparative evidence. Documented code/weight access and clearer applicability limits improve reproducibility and assessment. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, although Section 4.1 incorrectly claims normalized-AUC superiority over MLP-distill: Table 1 gives MotherNet 0.780 versus 0.802 for MLP-distill and 0.804 for XGBoost. Removing the ID-only leakage-confirmation results also weakens that particular analysis.
